name: Calculate performance and attribution against benchmarks
summary: Each month the performance team turns the closed net asset value into returns for the total fund, each investment department and each program, compares them with the Reference Portfolios and with risk-adjusted public market benchmarks, and explains the dollar value-added net of all costs. Analysts load index data and cost allocations, run the performance module, check hundreds of portfolios for anomalies and chase data breaks with fund accounting, then seniors reconcile to accounting income, attribute the value-added and draft a report the director approves. In quarter-end months the team waits for approved private valuations, calculates private program returns against lagged public benchmarks and prepares Board, statutory and incentive figures that the controller signs off. Data breaks, benchmark definitions, private asset lags and currency effects make the cycle slow and error-prone.

baseline.org_archetype: A national public pension investment manager of about 2,000 staff with an in-house 30-person performance group using SimCorp Dimension, spreadsheets and a data warehouse.
baseline.notes: Monthly flash results for management; final quarter-end results once private valuations are approved; fiscal year ends March 31.

trigger: Fund accounting releases the month-end net asset value.
end_state: The monthly performance report is published, and in quarter-end months the final quarterly returns and value-added are signed off and released to Board, statutory and compensation reporting.

volume.seasonality: Every third cycle is a quarter end with private valuations and Board reporting; the March cycle adds annual report and incentive calculations.

evidence.note: Monthly cycle per the organisation file; GIPS monthly total fund returns and quarterly private returns; statutory quarterly and annual reporting.

steps.name: Open cycle on NAV release
steps.description: When fund accounting releases the month-end net asset value, an analyst opens the monthly performance checklist, confirms the close is final for all portfolios, and notes any portfolios flagged as provisional by accounting.

error.defect_description: A portfolio still provisional in the close is treated as final.

evidence.note: Checklist-driven monthly production is typical; times are estimates.

steps.name: Load and check benchmark index returns
steps.description: Analysts load month-end levels and returns for the indexes behind the Reference Portfolios and every department and program benchmark from data vendors, in local currency and Canadian dollars, and check for missing values, late restatements and hedged versus unhedged series.

error.defect_description: Wrong index series (price instead of total return, or wrong hedge) used for a benchmark.

evidence.note: GIPS bars price-only benchmarks and requires benchmarks that reflect the mandate; CFA reading on benchmark validity. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Load cost allocations for net returns
steps.description: An analyst loads the month's operating, management fee and transaction cost allocations by department and program from Finance so that returns and value-added can be shown net of all costs, and checks totals against the expense ledger.

error.defect_description: Costs allocated to the wrong program.

evidence.note: The F2022 report states value-added is calculated net of all costs.

steps.name: Run return and benchmark calculations
steps.description: The performance module of the investment book of record runs overnight to calculate daily-linked time-weighted returns for every portfolio, program, department and the total fund, and the matching benchmark returns, in local currency and Canadian dollars.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors come from input data.

evidence.note: SimCorp Dimension performance measurement in-house; GIPS requires monthly time-weighted returns for total funds.

steps.name: Run reasonableness checks
steps.description: Analysts compare each portfolio's return with its exposures and market moves, look for outliers such as large returns on small portfolios, large cash flows on the wrong day, missing prices or currency mismatches, and run automated control reports across several hundred portfolios.

error.defect_description: A small mis-booking passes the tolerance and stays in the returns.

control.basis: Performance measurement policies and procedures: analytical review and reasonability checks before release

evidence.note: Job posting: analytical reviews and reasonability checks, investigate discrepancies, automated control checks. Break rate and hours are estimates.

steps.name: Raise data breaks with accounting and pricing
steps.description: An analyst writes up each break with the portfolio, amount and likely cause, such as a late trade booking, a stale external fund value or a portfolio mapped to the wrong program, and sends it to fund accounting or pricing operations to fix.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate of break handling effort.

steps.name: Correct bookings or prices behind breaks
steps.description: Fund accounting senior associates correct transactions, accruals or prices in the book of record, or confirm the number is right with an explanation, and tell performance when the portfolio can be recalculated.

error.defect_description: A correction introduces a new booking error.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: accounting corrections reviewed and approved

evidence.note: Corrections sit with fund accounting in the organisation file; times are estimates.

steps.name: Recalculate and re-check corrected portfolios
steps.description: After the overnight recalculation an analyst re-checks only the portfolios that had breaks, confirms each correction flowed through to returns and benchmark comparisons, and closes the tickets or reopens those still wrong.

error.defect_description: A correction is accepted without checking the knock-on effect on the parent program.

evidence.note: Re-check after correction follows the investigate-and-resolve duties in the job posting; times are estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile returns to accounting income
steps.description: A senior associate ties the total fund and department dollar returns to fund accounting's net income and change in net assets less net transfers from the pension plan, and explains or escalates any difference above tolerance.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Reconciliation of performance returns to audited accounting results

evidence.note: Reported returns and net income must agree in the annual report; the reconciliation step and its hours are estimates.

steps.name: Calculate Reference Portfolio and program benchmarks
steps.description: An analyst builds the Reference Portfolio returns from index returns at target weights and the department and program benchmarks from risk-adjusted combinations of public market indexes, with and without foreign currency effects, and checks benchmark changes against Board-approved definitions.

error.defect_description: Benchmark weight or leverage factor applied wrongly.

control.basis: Board-approved total Fund benchmarks; Management-developed department benchmarks

evidence.note: F2022 report: Board approves total Fund benchmarks; investment selection measured against comparable risk-adjusted passive public market benchmarks, reported excluding foreign currency.

steps.name: Compute value-added and attribution
steps.description: A senior associate calculates dollar and percentage value-added against the Reference Portfolios and splits the difference into the effect of the market risk target, diversification and leverage, balancing, and investment selection by department, with currency shown separately, for the month, year to date and five years.

error.defect_description: Linking or compounding error across periods in value-added.

evidence.note: F2022 report attributes five-year results to market risk (+3.1%), diversification and leverage (-1.9%) and investment selection (+2.7%); CFA reading on macro and micro attribution. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Send preliminary results to departments
steps.description: An analyst sends each investment department's business management team its preliminary returns, benchmark returns and value-added with a short list of drivers and asks for comments by a set date.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Job posting: prepare performance reports for investment groups and communicate results to stakeholders.

steps.name: Resolve department queries
steps.description: Departments question numbers that do not match their own estimates, such as a deal booked in the wrong month or a benchmark that missed a strategy change. A senior associate investigates each query and either explains it or sends the case back for recalculation.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Department review window and rework rate are estimates.

steps.name: Draft monthly performance report
steps.description: A senior associate drafts the monthly report for the CIO, senior management and Total Fund Management: total fund and department returns, benchmark returns, value-added, drivers and currency effects, with charts and a short commentary.

error.defect_description: Figure in the commentary does not match the tables.

evidence.note: Report content follows the organisation file's performance report object; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Director reviews report
steps.description: The performance director checks the key numbers against the reconciliation and last month's report, tests whether the commentary explains the value-added honestly, and approves or returns it with comments.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Management review and sign-off of performance reporting

evidence.note: Review effort and return rate are estimates.

steps.name: Publish monthly report
steps.description: An analyst distributes the approved report, loads the results to the reporting platform used by Total Fund Management and the departments, and archives the cycle evidence. In quarter-end months the work continues once the quarterly private valuations are approved.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Monthly reporting with private markets completed quarterly is common practice (WSIB); GIPS requires private market returns at least quarterly.

steps.name: Load quarter-end private valuations
steps.description: When the quarterly private valuations are approved and fund accounting re-releases the quarter-end net asset value, an analyst loads the new values, general partner capital account data and cash flows for private programs and checks that every holding has a current-quarter value.

error.defect_description: A holding left at the prior quarter value without a flag.

evidence.note: Quarterly valuations must be in the statements due within 45 days of quarter end, so the final quarter-end pass must finish around day 40; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Calculate private program returns with lagged benchmarks
steps.description: A senior associate calculates quarterly time-weighted and money-weighted returns for private equity, credit and real asset programs and compares them with their public market benchmarks, applying the agreed lag so that benchmark and valuation periods match.

error.defect_description: Benchmark lag inconsistent with the valuation period, distorting value-added.

evidence.note: GIPS: private market portfolios valued and returns calculated at least quarterly, money-weighted returns allowed; F2022 report measures private departments against public market benchmarks. Hours and lag convention are estimates.

steps.name: Finalise quarterly and five-year value-added
steps.description: The senior associate re-runs total fund and department attribution with the final private results and updates cumulative five-year dollar value-added used in the incentive plan and the Board's quarterly report, noting changes from the monthly flash.

error.defect_description: Five-year cumulative figure not rebased after a benchmark change.

control.basis: Incentive plan rules: five-year cumulative dollar value-added against the Reference Portfolios

evidence.note: F2022 report: total Fund performance multiplier uses five-year cumulative DVA (target C$8.2 billion); the Board receives quarterly value-add reports.

steps.name: Prepare Board and quarterly results inputs
steps.description: A senior associate prepares performance tables and commentary for the Board's quarterly package, the quarterly results release and, at fiscal year end, the annual report and compensation calculations.

error.defect_description: Table and narrative disagree across Board, release and annual report versions.

evidence.note: Board receives quarterly reports on returns and value-add; the Act requires quarterly statements and an annual report with performance against objectives.

steps.name: Director reviews quarter-end results
steps.description: The performance director reviews the final private returns, value-added and Board materials, checks consistency with the monthly flash and financial statements, and approves or sends items back.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Management review of quarter-end performance before Board reporting

evidence.note: Review effort and return rate are estimates.

steps.name: Controller signs off quarter-end performance
steps.description: The managing director and controller reviews the reconciliation of performance to the financial statements and signs off the figures that go to the Board, the stewards' quarterly statements and the public release.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Controller sign-off of results reported under the fund's governing act s. 50 and 51 (quarterly statements within 45 days, annual report within 60 days)

evidence.note: The Act sets the 45-day quarterly and 60-day annual reporting deadlines this sign-off serves; the sign-off role and times are estimates.

steps.name: Release quarter-end performance
steps.description: An analyst sends the signed-off figures to the Board secretariat for the Board package, to Finance for the quarterly statements and annual report, to Talent for incentive calculations and to Total Fund Management for capital allocation, and archives the evidence.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Recipients follow the organisation file's process map; timing is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Data breaks need recalculation
exceptions.description: Reasonableness checks or the accounting reconciliation find bookings, prices or mappings that are wrong; accounting fixes them and the calculation is re-run.

exceptions.name: Department disputes a result
exceptions.description: A department shows that a benchmark or allocation is wrong and the attribution is recalculated before the report.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end private results
exceptions.description: After the monthly flash the team waits for approved private valuations, computes private program returns with lagged benchmarks and prepares Board and statutory figures for controller sign-off.

exceptions.name: Fiscal year end
exceptions.description: The March cycle also produces annual report tables and the five-year value-added used for incentive multipliers, with extra review by Talent and the Board's committees.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from NAV release to report publication (final quarter-end release in quarter-end months)
benchmarks.population: Large Canadian public pension investment managers with in-house performance teams

evidence.note: Estimate: monthly results about eight business days after the NAV release; quarter-end results must be ready for statements due within 45 days of quarter end, so the final release comes about five weeks after the first NAV release.
the fund's governing act s. 50(1).

pain_points.description: Data breaks found after the close (late bookings, stale external values, mis-mapped portfolios) force recalculation loops with fund accounting.

evidence.note: Job posting stresses reasonability checks, investigating discrepancies and automated control checks.

pain_points.description: Private assets are valued quarterly and late, so monthly value-added for private departments is provisional and benchmark lags must be matched by hand.

evidence.note: GIPS quarterly valuation of private market portfolios; public pensions report private performance quarterly.

pain_points.description: Benchmark definitions, leverage adjustments and currency effects are complex, and departments dispute results tied to their incentive pay.

evidence.note: Value-added drives incentive multipliers; benchmark misspecification invalidates attribution.

pain_points.description: Figures are re-keyed into several report versions (management, Board, release, annual report), which creates consistency checks at every review.

evidence.note: Practitioner observation.

assumptions: One case is one monthly cycle for the whole fund; hands-on minutes are team totals summed across the analysts or seniors working on a step, so touch times are tens of hours. The simulator adds touch time to elapsed time as if one person did it, which overstates elapsed time for team steps; waits were set low to compensate, and the simulated monthly path (about 17 days from NAV release) is still longer than the estimated 12.

About 2 to 3 FTE of the 30-person performance group are on this production cycle; the rest work on analytics, benchmark design, private markets reporting, systems and ad hoc requests, which are outside this process.
Quarter-end months are modelled as the monthly flash followed by a final quarter-end pass once private valuations are approved; a third of cycles take the quarter-end path.
The benchmark lag convention for private programs (for example one quarter) is assumed, not taken from the organisation's disclosures.
Department business management teams review preliminary results; their time is not modelled here because their roles are outside this process in the organisation file.
fa_senior_accountant and fin_md_controller are in the organisation file but not in this process's role list there; they are added for correction work and quarter-end sign-off.
Hands-on times, waits and rework rates are tier C estimates unless a source is cited. Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file.
